picks.what: Woodcut in Hartmann Schedel’s Nuremberg Chronicle
picks.why: colored true view with the Minster (tower still unfinished) behind the walls on the Danube; two-page spread, so trimmed to the left-hand page, which holds the title and the Minster, to avoid the gutter

picks.what: Panorama, engraving in Braun and Hogenberg, Civitates Orbis Terrarum, vol. 1
picks.why: colored loose sheet, no fold; trimmed to the Ulm panel of the four-city plate (Nuremberg above, Salzburg and Lindau below): walled town with the Minster at its center

picks.file: Lange Städte in Deutschland Band 2 Nr. 24.jpg
picks.what: View from the southeast across the Danube, steel engraving
picks.why: river front with the Metzgerturm and the Minster with its unfinished tower; trimmed margins and caption

picks.what: The Minster and the Danube, photochrom print (Library of Congress)
picks.why: the newly completed Minster spire (1890) over the old town and the Danube bridge; color

picks.what: The old town across the Danube, photograph
picks.why: the classic view from Neu-Ulm: Minster, city wall, Metzgerturm and Danube; sharp, wide

gaps: P2: only plans (Merian 1643 #7, #10 1657). P5: only vertical military aerials (1920, #22–#24, map-like) and an undated etching of a single street (#21).
notes: #2: colored copy chosen over the sharper black-and-white #1 (also with a visible join in the middle); #3 is another colored copy with the gutter. #5: BnF dates its copy 1645; the Nuremberg–Ulm–Salzburg–Lindau plate is from vol. 1 (1572), as the Heidelberg copy (#8, a 2052 px colored strip of the same panel) is dated. P3 alternatives: #14 (1840, Minster from the Ziegellände), #11 (1818, Minster from the southeast, single building). P4: #16 is a copy of #15; #20 (‘about 1850’, wood engraving with the federal fortress) could be a second P4 view but its date is loose; #19 is an 1890 albumen photo. Not Ulm: #17 is New Ulm, Minnesota; #18 is Neu-Ulm (Bavaria). P6: modern ‘who’ is the Commons username, the only artist given; #27/#28 are drone shots of the railway station.
